Coordinator's recommendation is a comparison that keeps spontaneous access and advance certainty open. Panel A favors a physical board and walk-up reserve when spontaneous entry is the test focus. Panel B favors comparing anonymous time tokens with a physical board, retaining walk-up capacity, when advance certainty is the focus. Neither account supplies evidence for choosing that priority or proves an improvement.

Their useful difference is mechanism: a board communicates present status, while tokens attempt to allocate future access. The coordinator's proposed comparison would include the unchanged walk-up process as a baseline, alongside the board and tokens. This combines the accounts for assessment; it is not a new author revision or cross-panel consensus. Every candidate retains walk-up access and avoids names and accounts. Token allocation, recovery from lost tokens and protection of the reserve remain hypotheses requiring explanation.

C3-A2's remote-arrival objection is unresolved and decisive if advance certainty is prioritized: present availability cannot guarantee availability on arrival. C3-B3's objection about token maintenance is also unresolved; no burden observations establish that the addition is worthwhile. Neither objection can be settled by voting. The priority difference concerns user values; token reliability and maintenance concern mechanisms and evidence.

A smallest later tabletop comparison would apply the same simultaneous walk-up/advance claim, late arrival and reset scenarios to all three candidates. Record denied walk-ups, unsupported arrival promises, recovery steps and volunteer effort. Failure to protect the reserve disconfirms a candidate under the stated constraint; tokens with no certainty gain and additional work lack a demonstrated advantage. Stop after these scenarios without aggregating unlike benefits into a winner while priorities remain open. No test was performed.

The saved panels committed separately before seeing each other's accounts, but they share the same closed packet and investigators. That is source concentration, not independent corroboration. No observed priorities or outcomes are supplied, and no fresh facilitator checks occurred. This joint comparison closes the authorized exploration; all choices remain optional and pending.
